summary: A fully left-skewed tree requires a linear number of pointer changes to become a right-only chain. In-place predecessor splicing matches that bound with constant auxiliary storage.

optimality.argument: For an n-node left-skewed tree, each of the n - 1 left links must be cleared and replaced by a right link in the flattened result, requiring Omega(n) pointer mutations. In the current method, rightward advancement and predecessor searches follow each tree edge only a constant number of times across all splices, for O(n) total time and O(1) auxiliary pointer storage.

replacement_checks.evidence: Flattening an n-node left chain requires changing every one of its n - 1 non-null child links from left to right.
Every predecessor edge and flattened right-chain edge is traversed only a constant number of times, with a fixed set of node pointers.
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover branching, empty, and one-node trees; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
